column1: # Where each woven French plural in lex-fr.tsv was read.
# A noun row weaves its second form under an English plural, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. On 2026-10-08 every woven
# French plural was read in the headword line of English Wiktionary's French
# entry for its noun, rendered as a reader sees it, because the raw template
# mostly leaves the plural to Wiktionary's module: {{fr-noun|m}} prints
# "homme m (plural hommes)". All 178 are among the plurals their own noun's
# line prints, and none was changed.
# quote is the clause of that line which prints the plural, its qualifiers
# kept, or "invariable" where the line says the plural is the singular. A
# page holds every word of one spelling, so the clause is this word's own
# noun's, of the seed's gender and sense. Three pages hold two nouns of this
# spelling with different plurals: fils, son, is invariable where fils,
# threads, is the plural of fil; sol, floor, is "plural sols" where sol, the
# note of the scale, is invariable; and ciel, sky, is "plural cieux or
# ciels" where ciel, the canopy of a bed, is "plural ciels".
# tests/tools/plurals.test.ts requires every noun lex-fr.tsv weaves in a
# second form to have a line here with that form, citing the noun's own
# entry, its quote printing the form, and fails on a line outliving its row.
# ---- drafted from English Wiktionary via kaikki.org (dump of 2026-11-09), decided_by=wiktionary, status=proposed: woven, labelled, not yet read by a person ----
